extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation and catalyze research in universal speech representation learning. The benchmark includes a new general-purpose massively multilingual evaluation dataset dubbed Fleurs in 102 languages.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S combines multiple existing datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) and introduces a new dataset called Fleurs. Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark, using 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets in 102 languages. Between one and three recordings are collected for each sentence (2.3 on average), with new train-dev-test splits of 1509, 150 and 350 sentences respectively.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: For Fleurs: sentences from the FLoRes machine translation benchmark (dev and devtest sets). Other datasets source from: MLS (read audiobooks from Librivox), VoxPopuli (European Parliament sessions), CoVoST-2 (CommonVoice-based translation corpus), Minds-14 (e-banking intent classification).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Fleurs: new train-dev-test splits created with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets. For Minds-14: monolingual datasets are merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For speech retrieval: pool of transcription candidates augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Fleurs uses speech recordings collected for sentences from FLoRes with 2.3 recordings per sentence on average. Other datasets leverage existing annotations (transcriptions, translations, intents).
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For Fleurs: between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and fine-tuning scripts are made easily accessible through the HuggingFace platform. Additional test sets may be added in the future to confirm the generalization ability of submissions. A submission form will be provided where results can be double-checked for consistency. More details will be added on the XTREME-S Dataset card.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes speech recordings with speaker characteristics (speaker identity, language). For Fleurs-LangID, speakers are different between train sets and dev/test sets to avoid overfitting on speaker ID.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster. The benchmark aims to enable the community to build better speech representations in many languages, and enable rapid access to data-efficient speech technology for all the world's languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group (11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli. Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction for future work.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels. Significant performance gaps exist between different language families/geographical groups.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation and testing of multilingual speech representation models. Use cases include: speech recognition (ASR), speech-to-text translation (ST), speech classification (language identification, intent classification), and speech retrieval. Designed for few-shot learning and data-efficient self-supervised representation learning. Users should perform hyperparameter search and checkpoint selection on dev set, then report performance on test set.
